title: Google’s vice president comments on Google Pay launch in Uzbekistan
summary: Google’s vice president comments on Google Pay launch in Uzbekistan
detailed: Google’s vice president Doron Avni highlighted Uzbekistan's 2026 amendments to personal data protection legislation as a key factor enabling international technology services to enter the market, emphasizing flexible data storage regulations and cooperation with the United States on cybersecurity, cloud technologies and digital education.
Google's Vice President for Government Affairs and Public Policy in emerging markets, Doron Avni, announced the official launch of Google Pay in Uzbekistan in a post on LinkedIn.

Avni linked the launch of the payment service to changes in Uzbekistan's personal data protection legislation in 2026, which introduced a more flexible approach to data storage requirements based on data classification.
On October 27, Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration, announced the launch of Apple Pay and Google Pay payment services in Uzbekistan.
sentences: Google’s vice president Doron Avni highlighted Uzbekistan's 2026 amendments to personal data protection legislation as a key factor enabling international technology services to enter the market, emphasizing flexible data storage regulations and cooperation with the United States on cybersecurity, cloud technologies and digital education.
Google's Vice President for Government Affairs and Public Policy in emerging markets, Doron Avni, announced the official launch of Google Pay in Uzbekistan in a post on LinkedIn.

Avni linked the launch of the payment service to changes in Uzbekistan's personal data protection legislation in 2026, which introduced a more flexible approach to data storage requirements based on data classification.

According to Avni, Uzbekistan modernized its personal data protection legislation in 2026, replacing rigid requirements for storing data within the country with a more flexible approach based on data classification.
He stated that these changes created conditions for international technology services to enter Uzbekistan's market.
He also noted that clear regulations aligned with international standards allow global technologies to enter national markets more rapidly.
Avni stated that the launch of Google Pay was announced during U.S.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to Uzbekistan, which took place in the context of the C5+1 ministerial meeting held in Samarkand.
According to Avni, the visit demonstrated the shared aspirations of Uzbekistan and the United States to accelerate digital modernization.
The areas highlighted included strengthening national cybersecurity, developing cloud technologies and expanding digital education.
Avni expressed gratitude to the Government of Uzbekistan, U.S.
Ambassador to Uzbekistan Jonathan Henick and Google's team for their cooperation in implementing the project.
On October 27, Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration, announced the launch of Apple Pay and Google Pay payment services in Uzbekistan.
In October 2024, the government instructed relevant agencies to conduct negotiations regarding the integration of international payment services into Uzbekistan's payment systems.
The services included Alipay, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal and UniPay.

On January 20, 2026, the Legislative Chamber adopted a bill introducing amendments and additions to the Law "On Personal Data." During discussions, it was noted that the changes would serve to attract international payment systems, expand the market for digital services and create modern payment options for citizens and tourists.
